key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst combined with microalgae as a sacrificial agent substantially boosts solar-driven CO2 reduction to CO and CH4 while providing a carbon-negative capture-and-convert pathway.
engineering_relevance: The work points to a design strategy for more efficient photocatalytic CO2 conversion by coupling catalyst compositional engineering with a sustainable biomass-based reaction environment.
method: Designed an AB2O6-type high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy.
Used Cs and Ba to raise surface basicity for CO2 chemisorption, Bi for polarization and charge separation, and Nb/Ta for charge transport.
Compared photocatalytic CO2 conversion under three conditions: HEO alone, with microplastics, and with microalgae as sacrificial agents.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that adding microalgae increased CO and CH4 production by 10× and 4×, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: Practical deployment will depend on scalable microalgae handling and maintaining stable photocatalyst performance under real solar and reactor conditions.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
